sectors.title: Technology
sectors.summary: Technology is one of Ireland's fastest-growing sectors, home to the European headquarters of several of the world's largest technology companies as well as hundreds of Irish-founded ones. Roles range from software engineering and UX design to product management and data. You don't need to have studied computer science — many people enter through apprenticeships, conversion courses, or by switching from another field entirely.

sectors.title: Healthcare
sectors.summary: Healthcare covers medicine, nursing, physiotherapy, pharmacy, occupational therapy and many roles besides. It is one of the most stable career paths in the country, with strong demand across public and private settings. Routes in vary widely — from direct entry after the Leaving Certificate to postgraduate conversion programmes taken years later.

sectors.title: Law
sectors.summary: A legal career in Ireland can take several forms — solicitor, barrister, legal executive, or working in-house at a company. The traditional route is a law degree followed by professional exams, but graduate entry is also common, and a legal executive route exists that does not require a degree. Firms range from large international practices to small general practice in every county.

sectors.title: Finance
sectors.summary: Ireland's financial services sector is among the largest in Europe. Careers span banking, accountancy, insurance, fintech and the public sector. Routes in include professional accounting qualifications such as ACA, ACCA and CIMA — several of which you can earn while employed and paid — as well as direct graduate programmes.

sectors.title: Trades
sectors.summary: Skilled trades are among the most in-demand careers in Ireland. Entry is typically through a SOLAS apprenticeship: you are paid from the first year and there are no college fees. Trades offer strong long-term security, the option to become self-employed, and routes onward into site management, contracting and running your own business.

sectors.title: Media & communications
sectors.summary: Media and communications covers journalism, broadcasting, public relations, marketing and content. Ireland has a long tradition in journalism and broadcasting alongside a fast-growing digital and marketing industry. Routes in include journalism and communications courses, but increasingly also portfolios built independently.

sectors.title: Education
sectors.summary: Teaching, special education, youth work, further education and educational psychology. Primary teaching is usually a dedicated degree; secondary teaching is typically a subject degree followed by a professional masters. Youth and community work offers routes that do not require a traditional degree.

sectors.title: Engineering
sectors.summary: Civil, mechanical, electrical, biomedical and manufacturing engineering, among others. Ireland has particular strength in medical devices and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Entry is usually through a degree or a higher-level apprenticeship, and technician routes offer a paid way in without a four-year course.

sectors.title: Public sector
sectors.summary: The civil service, local authorities, An Garda Síochána, the Defence Forces, and state agencies. Many roles are filled by open competition rather than by degree requirement, and the Leaving Certificate is sufficient for a number of entry grades with structured promotion afterwards.

sectors.title: Other sectors
sectors.summary: Mentors whose work doesn't fit neatly into the categories above — including agriculture, hospitality, the arts, sport, logistics and the charity sector.
